Subject: LuminaHealth logging controls — decision timeline & evidence request

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and the asks we promised to surface from product/security so you can share with your team: 

1) Scope of logs: confirm whether your QA and production ingestion will require: request headers, full request bodies, response bodies, and any downstream error traces. Our ask: please indicate which of these must be retained for troubleshooting vs which must be redacted.

2) PII definition: you mentioned patient identifiers might appear in free-text prompts. Can you confirm the specific fields you consider PHI/PII (e.g., MRN, SSN, phone, email, insurance ID) so we can map sanitizer rules.

3) Trace/Correlation IDs: are you ok with deterministic hashing of trace IDs (per-customer salt) or do you require irreversible redaction? Any downstream need to re-associate traces for replay/forensics?

4) Retention & residency: target retention window for logs (30/90/365 days) and whether data must remain in us-east region only.

5) Evidence & access: please attach your security questionnaire and indicate whether your auditors need sample sanitized logs for tooling validation.

Next steps from our side: Marissa will follow up with a proposed redaction approach and a short SOW for a 4-week pilot; Sean will scope what we can reasonably expose as sanitized samples for your review.

Attachments: we didn't attach anything here — please send your questionnaire when you have it.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for the recap and fast turnaround. A few clarifications from our security team (Priya is copied):

- Scope: we need request headers (except auth tokens), response codes, and full request/response bodies for 30 days for debugging. After 30 days, metadata-only (status, latency, hash of trace id) is fine.
- PII: MRN, patient name, SSN, DOB, email, phone, and insurance ID must be redacted from stored logs. Free-text clinical notes may contain PHI — we'd like payload-level scrubbing to remove or mask tokens that match MRN/SSN patterns and to obfuscate patient names.
- Trace IDs: we prefer salted hashing (per-customer salt) so we can correlate events during the retention window but the raw trace ID cannot be recovered by anyone at rest.
- Residency: all logs must be stored in US regions (us-east preferred). No replication to EU/APAC.
- Evidence: attached is our security questionnaire (Lumina_Sec_Q_v3.pdf). For audit purposes we will need: an architecture diagram of your redaction pipeline, example sanitized payloads (dev samples), and confirmation you perform per-customer salts for any hashing.

We can share a small sample of anonymized logs if you provide a technical contact and a temporary SFTP or presigned URL. Can you propose a simple sample format and timeline? We're aiming to decide vendor and start pilot by the end of September.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform Security, LuminaHealth
Attachment: Lumina_Sec_Q_v3.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@luminahealth.com>, Priya Singh <priya.s@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LuminaHealth logging controls — decision timeline & evidence request

Alex — appreciate the detailed answers and the questionnaire. Quick response to each ask + proposed options so your security team can pick a preferred approach: 

A) Redaction approach options (summary):
  - Option 1 — deterministic salted hash for trace IDs (recommended): supports correlation during retention window, irreversible without salt, low compute.
  - Option 2 — irreversible redact (replace with UUID): strongest privacy guarantee; breaks cross-request correlation.
  - Option 3 — selective pseudonymization (hash & store mapping in KMS-backed vault for short-term rehydrate): allows replay for forensics but increases compliance burden.

B) Payload scrubbing:
  - We can configure token-based scrubbing rules (regex for MRN/SSN/phone/email) and a named-entity scrubber for patient names and free-text PHI. Rules are applied at ingestion before writing to long-term store.

C) Retention & region: configure a 30-day default retention for full logs, then roll to summarized metadata for 365 days. All storage can be pinned to us-east (single-region).

D) Evidence: attached a lightweight diagram and a 2-page summary of the scrub pipeline (proposed-redaction-approach.pdf, redaction-diagram.png). We can generate 3 dev sanitized samples (JSON) within 5 business days once you confirm a delivery method (SFTP or presigned S3 URL).

E) Pilot timeline: Jordan/Marissa propose a 4-week pilot starting mid-September, deliverables: implementation of scrub rules, 3 sanitized sample exports, and a short runbook for your auditors. If that works, we'll follow up with an SOW and estimated cost delta for the per-token logging retention.

Question for you: does Lumina require any additional cryptographic proof (e.g., HMAC salt rotation schedules) for hashed IDs, or is a per-customer static salt with lifecycle policy sufficient?

Thanks — let us know and we'll lock the pilot SOW.

Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-redaction-approach.pdf; redaction-diagram.png
